chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted until it was said, 'He does not break his fast,' then he broke his fast until it was said, 'He does not fast,' then he fasted the fast of David (peace be upon him): one day and one night (or one day and one night of rest), then he was commanded to fast three days in the month. He said: 'The fast of the whole year is equal to it, and it removes the heat of the chest.' Hammad said: I said, 'What is the heat of the chest?' He said, 'The heat of the chest is the whispering (of Satan).' Hammad said: I said, 'Which are the days?' He said: 'The first Thursday of the month, the first Wednesday after the tenth, and the last Thursday of it.' I said to him, 'Why did these days become the ones that are fasted?' He said: 'Indeed, those before us from the nations, when punishment was sent down upon one of them, it would descend on these fearful days.'

key_terms.صَوْمَ دَاوُدَ: The fast of David (one day fasting, one day rest)
key_terms.وَحَرِ الصَّدْرِ: Heat of the chest (interpreted as whispering/distraction)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific three days recommended for fasting in each month according to Imam al-Sadiq, and what is their spiritual significance?
ai.summary: In al-Isfahani’s al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Sunnah of the Prophet’s intermittent fasting, culminating in the specific recommendation to fast three days monthly to expel 'wahar' (spiritual distraction or whispering). The selection of these days—first Thursday, first Wednesday after the 10th, and last Thursday—is rooted in the historical precedent of divine punishment descending upon previous nations on these dates, thereby serving as a day of expiation and spiritual purification.
